documents: Published paper (PDF): Popkov & Popkov, Tectonics of the Basement of the Kara-Bogaz Arch (Turan Plate), Geotectonics 56(1), 55–64 (2022)

entry.evidence: The Kara-Bogaz geoblock is interpreted by many researchers as a structure underlain by the Precambrian sialic crust

steps.action: The authors take up the published rivals: a Precambrian (Baikalian/Cadomian) sialic crust under the geoblock (Leonov et al. and others), and an Upper Paleozoic folded complex merged with an intermediate structural complex.
steps.quote: According to Leonov et al. [16], all this may argue for the Cadomian (Baikalian) age of the consolidated crust in the Azov–Caspian segment.

steps.action: The authors recall their earlier South Mangyshlak result (weakly metamorphosed Paleozoic terrigenous basement intruded by Carboniferous granitoids, consistent with WNW aeromagnetic anomalies) as the analog for the present study.
steps.quote: this indicates the Paleozoic age of the rocks making up the basement of the South Mangyshlak petroleum-bearing region

steps.action: The authors pose the question of the nature of the Kara-Bogaz block and set out to systematize earlier opinions and refine its tectonic features.
steps.quote: The objective of the present work is to study the nature of the Kara-Bogaz block

steps.action: The authors compile earlier descriptions and K–Ar ages of the southern boreholes (Karshi amphibolites, microcline granites dated 440–240 Ma, porphyries dated 220 Ma).
steps.quote: Earlier studies by various researchers present the results of studying the compositions of the basement

steps.action: The authors give macroscopic and microscopic petrographic descriptions of cores from the northwestern boreholes, with logging-based correlation, including the Tamdy-1 granite–gneiss intervals.
steps.quote: we provide more detailed characteristics of the basement in this zone

steps.action: For the Tamdy-1 gneisses the authors state two rivals: xenoliths of older crust hosted by younger granites, or marginal facies of the pluton.
steps.quote: Probably, gneisses and crystalline schists were intruded by younger granites and are xenoliths hosted by an intrusive body.

steps.action: The authors compare the mineral composition and structure of the gneisses and schists and favour protomagmatic gneissic banding at the pluton margin.
steps.quote: giving grounds to consider gneisses as marginal facies of a granitic pluton

steps.action: The authors describe weakly metamorphosed terrigenous rocks (sandstones, conglomerates, charred plant detritus) in the upper basement of several boreholes.
steps.quote: Sporadically developed weakly metamorphosed terrigenous rocks in the upper part of the basement section constitute a geologic peculiarity of this region.

steps.action: The authors compare these rocks with the Upper Paleozoic lower molasse of South Mangyshlak and find them similar.
steps.quote: These rocks are similar in composition to Upper Paleozoic sediments from the Cape Peschany–Rakushechnaya Zone of the South Mangyshlak geoblock

steps.action: The weathered granite zone found in Bukbash-2 core is identified by electric logging below the molasse in six other boreholes.
steps.quote: an analogous zone was identified below it based on electric logging data

steps.action: The authors combine cited and Satpaev Institute K–Ar ages of granitoids and schists to estimate Late Devonian–Early Permian ages for the terminal Variscan tectonomagmatic phase.
steps.quote: The most probable age is Early Permian.

steps.action: Myospores found in Bukbash-2 metamorphic rocks give a paleontological age check independent of the radiometric dates.
steps.quote: these finds indicate the Paleozoic age of the host rocks.

steps.action: The authors describe cores and electric logs from the Kumsebshen-2 and Alamanel-1 reference boreholes in the adjoining Kumsebshen block (phyllitic schists, tuffs, metagenesis).
steps.quote: Based on our macroscopic examinations, these are black, solid, dense, silicified phyllitic units

steps.action: Using a 262 Ma age, the Kumsebshen units are correlated with the Upper Carboniferous–Lower Permian lower molasse of South Mangyshlak and of the northwestern arch.
steps.quote: These units are clearly correlated with the lower molasse complex of Upper Carboniferous‒Lower Permian age

steps.action: The authors reject the arguments for Precambrian age: high metamorphic grade is attributed to contact overprint near intrusions (Oimasha analog), amphibolites to apo-igneous greenschist rocks, and the 440 Ma ages to K–Ar scatter.
steps.quote: the local increase in the degree of metamorphic alteration in rocks may be related to the proximity of intrusive bodies

steps.action: From the magnetic field heterogeneity, gravity data and adjacent geology, the authors infer terrigenous (NE) and effusive (SW) zones and compile a schematic basement structure map.
steps.quote: Employing geological data on adjacent areas, as well as magnetic and gravity survey data, we compiled a map schematically showing the structure of this region

steps.action: The authors note that NW-oriented magnetic anomalies, characteristic of Paleozoic structures, were found in the part of the arch covered by their earlier aeromagnetic survey.
steps.quote: Magnetic anomalies with the same orientation have been revealed in the northwestern part of the arch

steps.action: The authors keep the claim that the geoblock is a Hercynian megaanticlinorium of active-margin rocks, while allowing that Precambrian fragments may be present.
steps.quote: We consider the Kara-Bogaz geoblock to be a Hercynian megaanticlinorium of the young Turan Plate

tree.answer: Repeated across 23 boreholes and the South Mangyshlak analog
Partly: paleontology, logging in other boreholes, and the adjacent Kumsebshen block agree
Hercynian megaanticlinorium; Precambrian fragments not excluded

end.claim: The Kara-Bogaz geoblock is a Hercynian megaanticlinorium of greenschist-grade active-margin sedimentary and volcanosedimentary rocks intruded by Late Paleozoic granitoids, with no direct evidence of pre-Paleozoic crust, though Precambrian fragments may exist.

decisive_move.sentence: Reinterpreting the high metamorphic grade (the only argument for Precambrian age) as contact overprint near granitoid intrusions removes the support for the rival Precambrian crust.

gates.evidence: The cores come from existing petroleum exploration boreholes, not from drilling directed by a hypothesis (p. 57). Paleontological and K–Ar ages could in principle have shown pre-Paleozoic rocks (p. 60), but the Precambrian rival is left open (p. 62). Nothing was fixed in advance.

novelty_claims.quote: The data on the other boreholes had not been studied and, in this respect, we provide more detailed characteristics of the basement in this zone.

limits: No review file was supplied. Pre-review changes are not visible, although reviewers are thanked (p. 62). The paper does not state which K–Ar dates are new: the Satpaev Institute dating may have been commissioned or may have been earlier work (inference). No uncertainties are given for most ages. No U–Pb zircon or geochemical data are used. The method behind the Fig. 3 map is not described. Core is unavailable for many intervals (p. 60). The Precambrian rival is disputed but not shown wrong, so the outcome is kept, not contradicted. Sub-claims: the gneisses as protomagmatic gneissic banding are best_explanation (p. 61); the Early Permian age of the terminal tectonomagmatic phase is an estimate without stated resolution (p. 60); the NE terrigenous / SW effusive zoning from magnetic data is an assumption (p. 61); the lower molasse correlation is best_explanation (p. 60). New magnetometric data are said to be needed (p. 62).

disagreements.target: Leonov et al. [16] and others: Baikalian/Precambrian consolidated crust under the Kara-Bogaz geoblock
disagreements.support: Core petrography, K–Ar and myospore ages, and the contact-metamorphism reinterpretation show no direct pre-Paleozoic evidence.
disagreements.quote: Our research within the Kara-Bogaz Arch indicate the absence of any direct geological evidence for the presence of the continental crust older than Paleozoic

disagreements.target: Earlier geophysical basis for Precambrian geoblocks occupying 60–75% of the Turan Plate [1, 3, 5, 12]
disagreements.support: The authors note that the conclusion rests on imprecise geophysics and scarce drilling.
disagreements.quote: earlier geophysical studies (which were; however, not quite precise)

disagreements.target: Knyazev et al. [8, 9]: Precambrian age of the Karshi amphibolites inferred from high metamorphic grade
disagreements.support: The amphibolites are interpreted as apo-igneous greenschist rocks overprinted by granitoid heat, with the Oimasha analog.
disagreements.quote: so that they cannot serve as an argument for the Precambrian age.

disagreements.target: Interpretation of the Tamdy-1 gneisses as regional amphibolite-facies (Proterozoic) rocks [9, 16]
disagreements.support: Gneisses alternate with schists of similar mineralogy and structure and are taken as marginal facies of the pluton.
disagreements.quote: suggesting that gneisses represent marginal facies of the granitoid pluton recovered by borehole Tamdy-1

disagreements.target: K–Ar ages of ca. 440 Ma for Karshi granitoids as evidence of older crust [8]
disagreements.support: The dates are singular among abundant Devonian–Carboniferous granitoids and scatter strongly; method accuracy is questioned.
disagreements.quote: we should not exclude that such scatter is caused by insufficient accuracy of the method itself.

alternatives_considered.chosen: Gneisses as marginal facies of the granite pluton (protomagmatic gneissic banding)
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Gneisses and schists as xenoliths in a younger intrusive body
alternatives_considered.reason: Similar [...] composition and structural features of gneisses and crystalline schists

alternatives_considered.chosen: High metamorphic grade due to contact thermal overprint near intrusions
alternatives_considered.alternatives: High metamorphic grade indicating Precambrian age
alternatives_considered.reason: Proximity of intrusive bodies; Oimasha area analog in South Mangyshlak

alternatives_considered.chosen: Karshi age scatter possibly caused by K–Ar method inaccuracy
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Two granitoid generations, the older Silurian–Ordovician, as a xenolith body [8]
alternatives_considered.reason: Ages sharply differ (440, 352, 313, 310 Ma) amid abundant Devonian–Carboniferous granitoids
